title: Part 3 — Conversation 1: an indemnity clause the client won't sign
instructionsVi: Ở mục tiêu 900, hội thoại dùng đăng ký ngôn ngữ pháp lý và câu hỏi hàm ý chiếm ít nhất một trong ba câu.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 32 through 34.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Procurement have come back on clause eleven. They won't accept an unlimited indemnity.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Nobody accepts an unlimited indemnity. What are they proposing instead?

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: A cap at twelve months' fees. Which on this contract is about four hundred thousand.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: And our exposure if the data centre goes down is what, three million? I've seen that number somewhere.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Two point eight, in the risk register. So the cap doesn't cover us.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: It doesn't cover us on paper. Whether it ever gets tested is another question — we've had one claim in nine years.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: I'd rather not price nine years of luck into a five-year contract.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Fair. Go back and ask for the cap to sit at twice the annual fee, with data-loss events carved out entirely. If they refuse the carve-out, escalate it to me before you concede anything.

questions.prompt: 32. What is the client refusing to agree to?

options.text: An indemnity with no upper limit.
A five-year contract term.
An increase in the annual fee.
The use of an external data centre.

questions.explanationVi: 'They won't accept an unlimited indemnity'. Các phương án còn lại đều lấy từ có xuất hiện trong bài (five-year, fee, data centre) nhưng không phải điều bị từ chối.

questions.prompt: 33. What does the woman imply when she says, "I'd rather not price nine years of luck into a five-year contract"?

options.text: The contract should be shortened to nine months.
A clean claims history is not a safe basis for accepting the cap.
The pricing team should recalculate the annual fee.
Previous claims were settled for too little.

questions.explanationVi: Người đàn ông vừa lập luận 'chín năm chỉ có một vụ khiếu nại', tức lấy quá khứ may mắn làm căn cứ. Câu nói của cô ấy bác bỏ chính lập luận đó. Câu hỏi hàm ý luôn phải đọc ngược lên lượt thoại ngay trước.

questions.prompt: 34. What does the man instruct the woman to do if the carve-out is refused?

options.text: Accept the twelve-month cap.
Withdraw from the negotiation.
Bring the matter to him before conceding.
Update the risk register.

questions.explanationVi: 'escalate it to me before you concede anything' — 'escalate' ở đây nghĩa là chuyển lên cấp trên, không phải 'leo thang'.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 2: prorating a licence fee (ba người nói)
format: TOEIC Listening — Part 3 · Conversation 2 (câu 35–37), ba người nói
instructionsVi: Hội thoại ba người: phải theo dõi ai chịu trách nhiệm việc gì, vì câu hỏi thường hỏi 'người đàn ông thứ hai sẽ làm gì'.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation among three speakers and answer questions 35 through 37.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: The Halloran renewal starts on the eighteenth, not the first. Do we bill them for a full month?

transcript.speaker: M1
transcript.text: No — anything starting mid-cycle gets prorated. Thirteen days out of thirty-one.

transcript.speaker: M2
transcript.text: That's how we've always done it, but the new agreement supersedes the old one, and I don't think the proration wording survived the redraft.

transcript.speaker: M1
transcript.text: Seriously? So we'd be entitled to charge a full month?

transcript.speaker: M2
transcript.text: Entitled, yes. Whether we should is a different conversation. They're a nine-year account.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: I'd rather not test that on a renewal. Bill the thirteen days and note it as a goodwill application of the old terms.

transcript.speaker: M2
transcript.text: Then I'll draft a one-line side letter so it doesn't set a precedent. Give me until Thursday.

transcript.speaker: M1
transcript.text: And I'll hold the invoice until the letter's signed.

questions.prompt: 35. What problem does the second man identify?

options.text: The renewal date has been recorded incorrectly.
The client has not paid the previous invoice.
The new agreement may no longer contain a proration clause.
The account has been open for less than a year.

questions.explanationVi: 'the new agreement supersedes the old one, and I don't think the proration wording survived the redraft'. 'Survive' ở đây nghĩa là còn được giữ lại trong bản mới.

questions.prompt: 36. What does the woman decide?

options.text: To charge only for the thirteen days as a gesture of goodwill.
To charge for the full month as the new contract allows.
To postpone the renewal to the first of next month.
To cancel the invoice altogether.

questions.explanationVi: 'Bill the thirteen days and note it as a goodwill application of the old terms'. (B) là điều họ CÓ QUYỀN làm nhưng đã chọn không làm — bẫy kinh điển của Part 3 mức cao.

questions.prompt: 37. What will the second man do by Thursday?

options.text: Hold the invoice.
Draft a side letter.
Contact the client directly.
Redraft the whole agreement.

questions.explanationVi: Hai người đàn ông nhận hai việc khác nhau: M2 soạn thư phụ lục, M1 giữ hoá đơn. (A) là việc của người kia.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 3: staff attrition at a distribution centre
instructionsVi: Câu hỏi suy luận về nguyên nhân: dữ kiện nằm rải ở ba lượt thoại khác nhau.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 38 through 40.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: We're down eleven pickers since March and we've only replaced four.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Is that attrition or are we losing them to the new fulfilment centre?

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Both, but mostly the second. They're paying about eighty pence an hour more and they run fixed shifts.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: We could match the rate. We can't match fixed shifts — our volume moves week to week.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Then match the rate and give people their rota four weeks out instead of two. Half the exit interviews mention not being able to plan childcare.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Four weeks is a big ask for planning. Let me see whether the forecast is stable enough at three.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Three would help. It's the uncertainty people leave over, not the shifts themselves.

questions.prompt: 38. According to the man, what is the main reason staff are leaving?

options.text: Natural attrition and retirement.
A competing employer offering better pay and hours.
Poor conditions inside the warehouse.
The closure of the distribution centre.

questions.explanationVi: 'Both, but mostly the second' — 'the second' trỏ về 'losing them to the new fulfilment centre'. Phải nối đại từ với lượt thoại trước mới trả lời được.

questions.prompt: 39. Why does the woman say the company cannot offer fixed shifts?

options.text: The union agreement forbids it.
There are not enough supervisors.
Workload varies from week to week.
The rota software does not support it.

questions.explanationVi: 'our volume moves week to week' — 'volume' ở đây là khối lượng hàng, không phải âm lượng.

questions.prompt: 40. What compromise is being considered?

options.text: Publishing the rota three weeks in advance.
Reducing the number of pickers needed.
Offering a one-off retention bonus.
Transferring staff to the fulfilment centre.

questions.explanationVi: Người đàn ông đề xuất bốn tuần, người phụ nữ đề nghị xem xét ba tuần và người kia đồng ý. Đáp án nằm ở con số CUỐI CÙNG được thống nhất, không phải con số đầu tiên nghe thấy.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 4: a forfeited deposit (có bảng biểu)
format: TOEIC Listening — Part 3 · Conversation 4 (câu 41–43), có bảng tra cứu
instructionsVi: Câu 'Look at the graphic' đòi hỏi ghép thông tin nghe được với một dòng trong bảng — thông tin cần ghép không bao giờ được đọc thẳng ra.
promptEn:
Listen to the conversation, look at the table, and answer questions 41 through 43.

WESTGATE HALL — CANCELLATION SCHEDULE

Notice given before the event | Deposit retained by the venue
More than 90 days | 0%
61–90 days | 25%
31–60 days | 50%
30 days or fewer | 100%

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: We're moving the conference to the Riverside site, so I need to cancel Westgate. The event was the twelfth of November.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: And today is the twentieth of September. That's fifty-three days.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Fifty-three. So we forfeit half the deposit — three thousand of the six.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Unless we get the notice in before the end of the month. Then we'd be at sixty-one days and drop a band.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: The end of the month is ten days away. Fifty-three plus ten is sixty-three days before the event? No — cancelling later means fewer days, not more.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: You're right, I had that backwards. Sixty-one days would have meant cancelling twelve days ago.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: So there's nothing to gain by waiting, and something to lose if this drags past the twelfth of October. Send it today.

questions.prompt: 41. Look at the table. What percentage of the deposit will the venue keep?
questions.explanationVi: 53 ngày nằm trong khoảng 31–60 ngày → giữ lại 50%. Người phụ nữ cũng xác nhận '£3.000 trên £6.000', tức đúng một nửa.

questions.prompt: 42. What mistake does the man make?

options.text: He gives the wrong date for the event.
He assumes waiting would increase the number of days' notice.
He confuses the deposit with the full hire fee.
He books the wrong venue.

questions.explanationVi: Anh ta nghĩ đợi đến cuối tháng sẽ 'lên 61 ngày', trong khi càng đợi thì số ngày báo trước càng ÍT. Chính anh ta thừa nhận 'I had that backwards'.

questions.prompt: 43. Why does the woman want to send the notice immediately?

options.text: The Riverside site requires confirmation today.
The deposit is refundable only in September.
Delay cannot help and could push them into a worse band.
The venue manager is away from next week.

questions.explanationVi: 'nothing to gain by waiting, and something to lose if this drags past the twelfth of October' — mốc 12/10 chính là ranh giới rơi xuống mức giữ 100%.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 5: a site-visit waiver (ba người nói)
format: TOEIC Listening — Part 3 · Conversation 5 (câu 44–46), ba người nói
instructionsVi: Ba người nói với hai giọng nam gần nhau: bám vào nội dung công việc của từng người thay vì cố phân biệt giọng.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation among three speakers and answer questions 44 through 46.

transcript.speaker: M1
transcript.text: The visitors arrive at nine. Have they all returned the liability waiver?

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Six of the eight. The two outstanding are from the parent company, and they're arguing they're covered by the group policy.

transcript.speaker: M2
transcript.text: The group policy covers employees on our sites. It doesn't replace the waiver — the waiver is what gets them past the gate.

transcript.speaker: M1
transcript.text: Can they sign on arrival?

transcript.speaker: M2
transcript.text: They can, but then they'd need the safety briefing before signing, and the briefing runs twenty minutes. That eats into the tour.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Or I send the form now and ask them to sign before they board. It's a two-hour flight; there's time.

transcript.speaker: M1
transcript.text: Do that. And print two spares — someone always turns up with the wrong signature block.

questions.prompt: 44. Why have two visitors not returned the form?

options.text: They believe an existing group policy makes it unnecessary.
They did not receive the email.
They are not attending the visit.
They are waiting for their manager's approval.

questions.explanationVi: 'they're arguing they're covered by the group policy'. Động từ 'argue' báo hiệu đây là lập luận của họ chứ chưa chắc đúng — và đúng là bị bác ngay lượt sau.

questions.prompt: 45. What is the drawback of signing on arrival?

options.text: The gate closes at nine o'clock.
A required briefing would shorten the tour.
The forms cannot be printed on site.
The insurer must approve each signature.

questions.explanationVi: 'the briefing runs twenty minutes. That eats into the tour'. 'Eat into' = lấn vào, làm hao thời gian.

questions.prompt: 46. What will the woman do?

options.text: Deliver the safety briefing herself.
Contact the group insurer.
Send the form to be signed before the flight.
Postpone the visit by one day.

questions.explanationVi: 'I send the form now and ask them to sign before they board' — 'board' là lên máy bay, được xác nhận bởi 'It's a two-hour flight'.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 6: an unreconciled bank statement
instructionsVi: Hội thoại có con số: đáp án thường là con số KHÔNG được nói thẳng mà phải trừ hai số nghe được.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 47 through 49.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: August won't reconcile. The ledger says forty-one thousand two hundred; the statement says forty thousand four hundred.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Eight hundred out. Any single transaction that size?

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Two at four hundred, both to the same supplier, both on the thirty-first.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Then it's almost certainly a duplicate posting rather than a missing payment. Did the bank take one or two?

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: One. So we've recorded a payment we never made.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: Reverse the second entry and leave a note against it. And check September before you close August — if the duplicate was cloned from a template, it'll be there too.

questions.prompt: 47. What is the size of the discrepancy?
questions.explanationVi: 41.200 − 40.400 = 800, và người đàn ông nhắc lại 'Eight hundred out'. (A) là giá trị từng giao dịch, không phải mức lệch.

questions.prompt: 48. What does the man conclude is the cause?

options.text: A payment was never sent to the supplier.
The bank charged an unexpected fee.
The same payment was entered twice in the ledger.
The supplier invoiced the wrong amount.

questions.explanationVi: 'a duplicate posting rather than a missing payment' — chính (A) là phương án anh ta LOẠI TRỪ. Nghe câu có 'rather than' thì vế sau luôn là cái bị loại.

questions.prompt: 49. What does the man ask the woman to check?

options.text: The supplier's bank details.
The following month's entries.
Last year's August figures.
The template used for invoices.

questions.explanationVi: 'check September before you close August'. (D) gần đúng — mẫu được nhắc tới — nhưng anh ta yêu cầu kiểm tra tháng Chín, không phải kiểm tra cái mẫu.

title: Part 3 — Conversation 7: outside the committee's remit
instructionsVi: Cuộc trao đổi có xung đột ngầm: đáp án đúng thường mô tả thái độ chứ không mô tả sự việc.
promptEn: Listen to the conversation and answer questions 50 through 52.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: The steering committee has voted to cut the trial price by fifteen per cent.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: They've voted to recommend it, I hope. Pricing sits outside their remit.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: The minutes say 'resolved', not 'recommended'.

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Then the minutes are wrong, and I'd rather correct them now than argue about it in November. Their terms of reference are two years old but they haven't been superseded.

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.text: I'll ask the secretary to reissue the minutes. Do you want the fifteen per cent looked at on its merits?

transcript.speaker: W
transcript.text: Yes — separately, and through the pricing group. If the number is right it'll survive being asked for properly.

questions.prompt: 50. What is the woman's objection?

options.text: The committee has no authority to decide prices.
A fifteen per cent cut is too large.
The trial should be cancelled.
The minutes were circulated too late.

questions.explanationVi: 'Pricing sits outside their remit' — 'remit' là phạm vi trách nhiệm. Cô ấy KHÔNG phản đối con số 15%, điều được chứng minh ở lượt cuối.

questions.prompt: 51. Why does the woman mention November?

options.text: The trial ends in November.
She prefers to settle the point before it becomes contentious later.
The committee next meets in November.
The terms of reference expire in November.

questions.explanationVi: 'I'd rather correct them now than argue about it in November' — tháng Mười Một chỉ đại diện cho 'về sau', không phải một mốc sự kiện. Ba phương án kia đều gán cho nó một sự kiện không hề được nói.

questions.prompt: 52. What does the woman agree to?

options.text: Accepting the committee's decision as recorded.
Rewriting the committee's terms of reference.
Considering the price cut through the proper group.
Delaying the trial until the minutes are corrected.

questions.explanationVi: 'separately, and through the pricing group'. Cô ấy tách bạch hai chuyện: sai thẩm quyền và giá trị của đề xuất.
